reviews.title: Fantastic Design and Quality, but Too Small
reviews.comment: I’m going to give this mouse 5 stars, even though I won’t be using it. It is exactly what is pictured. The internal LED is very well-diffused and easy to customize with Gravastar’s software. The sensor is extremely accurate. The mouse has negligible latency in both configurations, and is very smooth across my mousepad. The buttons feel excellent, and the ergonomics are pretty good: buttons are where you need them to be without being in the way. Why won’t I be using it then? The size. It’s too small for me. I was very sad when I gave it a try, and it just didn’t fill my hand as well as my other mouse (Razer DeathAdder V2 X). Gravastar is a fantastic company that makes quality products with a distinct style. I love their keyboard, their chargers, and their speakers. My wife has the Sakura pink version of this mouse that matches her keyboard, and she LOVES it. So I would recommend this mouse on the basis of its quality and its style to anyone, with the caveat that it’s just not the best fit for larger hands. If you’re used to a smaller mouse like a Logitech, then maybe this would be close to what you’re used to anyway, but for me, I’m more comfortable on my DeathAdder.
reviews.author: Silas Growden

reviews.title: Buy under $80 and you get an absolute GEM
reviews.comment: Beautiful mouse. The webby design is beautiful but on the right side for Claw and Fingertip Grips makes for a very awkward seat for the fingers, palm grip is not an issue because there are grated flat surfaces toward the front of each side that is very accommodating for the thumb and fingers but I personally like to grip with my fingertips curled around the side, fingertips sitting vertically in the middle rather than fully straight and riding horizontally along the side. This completely avoids that surface meant for fingers and relies on the webbed design for support which is a little off feeling. By no means does this make it unusable, you just have to get used to it. My ring fingertip generally makes contact with that grated support surface but my pinky sits further back and I have to set it on the skinny web part. This does not make the mouse unusable I just believe it justifies $60 over $80, this oddity in the design applies to all of GravaStar's mice. Overall the PAW3395 is the best widespread sensor to date, yes there are better sensors but they are not generational leaps, they're just small improvements and support gimmicks like 4k and 8k polling when there is no proven practical increase over 2K, the specs of this mouse and the quality of the wireless (and bluetooth)- are pretty unbeatable at $60, $80 I'd say if you really want the design of this mouse, go for it, but this thing is always on sale. For anyone wondering visually the transparent material is very high quality, it really does not feel or look like "Clear plastic" this is very dense, very solid and very pretty looking material and the way it's made to be clear is so well done I really can't take my eyes off it when I'm using it, so don't worry on that front, it will please you. For anyone wondering about the RGB, it's good, but the pictures are very true to real life, the RGB will not be brighter in person and light up the whole mouse, it will shine very prettily through the surrounding transparent area, but from where the mouse clicks start and forward are not affected by the RGB at all and just remain transparent, however, any outside lightsource like your room, the sun or your monitor will make this thing shine so beautifully especially during movement. I can't say much on battery life but that's cause I've had it for over a week and haven't had to charge it since I charged it initially out of the box, so it must be good, I spend alot of time with it daily as well. Clicks are great, very snappy very light, they feel instant due to the lack of pre and post travel, they pretty much have off and on. Side buttons have a slight bit of post travel but me personally I find that to be ideal for side buttons in particular as it allows for a smoother spam as opposed to main clicks which benefit from little pre and post travel. Overall I bought this mouse hoping it would be really good, but skeptical due to the lack of reviews of this particular model (Transparent Black)- and was afraid it would feel cheap or not at pretty as advertised, or rely too heavily on the design and not really serve as a good mouse in function, and I did. I got the prettiest mouse in my collection of like 30, has the highest specs in the practical zone of new mice, and all of this for like 65 after tax. (I own mice that go to 4K, 30-42k DPI, there is zero difference in this to them compared to going from 1K to 2K or 18000 DPI to 26000DPI.)- Do not overlook the grip issue though it really is a learning curve unless you're just a really carefree person. I had to get used to resting my pinky on a skinny vertical bar instead of a flat surface, but again, if you palm your mouse you'll have zero issues. Also if you claw/fingertip with your fingers gripping the front of the mouse rather than the middle or back of the side, you're equally as good to go.

reviews.title: Beautiful but!
reviews.comment: The only problem for me it is too narrow from the sides making it hard for your palm to hold it!! You need to bring your palm of your hand really close in order to hold a grip! And it was a deal breaker for me and thats the only reason I returned this mouse! Otherwise, its a really good mouse! The weight is perfect not too heavy and not too light! It has all the functions and side buttons a gamer needs! Good website key customization! Really easy and convenient! Battery life was good! Durable and made well for gamers. The LED is one of the best I have seen on a mouse!!
